impDef.description: The set of collations supported by an SQL-implementation. These may be defined by a standard or by the SQL-implementation itself. Each supported collation has a name, its definition, the list of character sets to which it can be applied, and whether or not padding with spaces is to be used when comparing two strings of unequal length.
The set of character repertoires supported by an SQL-implementation.
The set of character encoding forms supported by an SQL-implementation. These may be defined by a standard or by the SQL-implementation itself.
Whether the DEFINITION_SCHEMA referenced by an INFORMATION_SCHEMA describes schemas in catalogs other than the catalog in which the INFORMATION_SCHEMA is located.
Whether the default collation for the UCS character repertoire is UCS_BASIC or UNICODE.
The values of the CONSTRAINT_CATALOG, CONSTRAINT_SCHEMA, and CONSTRAINT_NAME columns in the TABLE_CONSTRAINTS base table when a constraint name was not supplied when the constraint was created.
Any additional character sets supported by an SQL-implementation.
The maximum length of an identifier.
The maximum length of a variable-length character string type.
The maximum value of INTEGER data type.
The items that are represented in the table SQL_IMPLEMENTATION_INFO.
The contents of the row in the CHARACTER_ENCODING_FORMS base table describing a character encoding form defined by an SQL-implementation.
The contents of the row in the CHARACTER_REPERTOIRES base table describing a character repertoire defined by an SQL-implementation.
The contents of the row in the CHARACTER_SETS base table describing a character set defined by an SQL-implementation.
The contents of the row in the COLLATIONS base table describing a collation defined by an SQL-implementation.
The contents of the row in the COLLATION_CHARACTER_SET_APPLICABILITY base table describing an additional applicability of a collation to a character set.

The the values of the CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH, CHARACTER_OCTET_LENGTH, CHARACTER_SET_CATALOG, CHARACTER_SET_SCHEMA, CHARACTER_SET_NAME, COLLATION_CATALOG, COLLATION_SCHEMA, and COLLATION_NAME columns in the DATA_TYPE_DESCRIPTOR base table when the schema is INFORMATION_SCHEMA and the data type is some character string type.
